correctness.rationale: For \(v\) in part \(V_i\), the closed-neighborhood sum is exactly \(w-s_i+f(v)\), so the part constraints reduce to the single worst label \(\mu_i\) and are equivalent to \(w-s_i+\mu_i\ge1\). For fixed total weight \(w\), the three disjoint local cases are: a part containing \(-1\), which requires \(s_i\le w-2\); a part with no \(-1\) but at least one zero, which requires \(s_i\le w-1\); and the all-\(+1\) part, which requires \(n_i\le w\). These are exactly the three truncated generating-polynomial terms in the package, and coefficient extraction enforces the global total weight. The lower summation limit is also proved: if \(w\le0\), no part can be all \(+1\), hence \(s_i\le w-1\) for every part and summing contradicts \(r\ge2\). A fresh independent brute-force replay over all 23 nondecreasing multipartite profiles of orders two through six matched the literal definition and structural criterion; the unbounded theorem rests on the symbolic argument, not that finite replay.
